newsitem.title: LEBANON: Beirut to complain about Israeli shelling - Minister.
newsitem.headline: Beirut to complain about Israeli shelling - Minister.

text.p: Lebanon will lodge a complaint with a five-nation monitoring group over Israeli shelling of a southern Lebanese village on Tuesday, Foreign Minister Faris Bouez said.
"This shelling is a violation of the April understanding and therefore we will file a complaint to the monitoring group," Bouez told reporters in Beirut.

The monitoring group -- comprising the United States, France, Syria, Lebanon and Israel -- was formed under an April 26 ceasefire understanding that ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon last year in which about 200 people died.
Early on Tuesday, guerrillas of the pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) fired mortar bombs into 13 pro-Israeli militia outposts but no casualties were reported, pro-Israeli security sources said.

In apparent retaliation, Israeli gunners shelled the south Lebanon village of Kfar Roumman facing the 15-km (nine-mile)- wide Israeli occupation zone, Lebanese security sources said. There was no word on casualties in the shelling.

The monitoring group has previously held Israel responsible three times for shelling south Lebanon villages and said the acts violated the terms of the ceasefire understanding which banned firing from or at civilian targets.
The understanding however did not ban guerrillas from attacking Israeli troops and their allies which control the south Lebanon buffer strip.
